load.why: Thread llama-server runs at 98% while the GPU is 2% busy. Everything waits on this one thread; use --cpu-profile to see what it does.

warmup.why: GPU 39% busy while thread llama-server runs at 76%: the host is working or spinning on a wait during the GPU's idle part. --nsys shows the gaps, --cpu-profile what the host does.

serve_c1.why: GPU 71% busy with nothing else saturated, so the rest of the time is host work or synchronization. --nsys shows the gaps, --cpu-profile what the host does.

serve_c4.why: GPU 76% busy with nothing else saturated, so the rest of the time is host work or synchronization. --nsys shows the gaps, --cpu-profile what the host does.

memory.text: 10.04 GiB of mapped files stay in RAM during serve. These pages are reclaimable page cache, not a leak, but they are why a later run loads fast and why the machine shows little free RAM.
Host memory grew 912 MiB during serve, from 1.70 GiB to 2.59 GiB. If it keeps growing with more requests it is a leak or an unbounded cache; if it levels off, a cache filling up.
195.79 GiB of the model stays in host buffers, not on a GPU. CPU work reads it from there, so with mmap it depends on the page cache, and the disk when the cache has been evicted.

movement.text: The model is on hdd storage (<path>/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-Q8_0-upstream.gguf). This run did not read it from disk; --cold-start measures what a first load costs.
The model was 100% in the page cache, so this load time is a warm one. A cold start reads it from disk and takes longer.

serving.text: Going from 1 to 4 concurrent requests raised throughput 2.26 times, and the median first token moved from 597 to 1,695 ms.
